baslik: 208 Seconds: How Geese Took Out Both Engines of Flight 1549

sahneler.metin: Both engines died at under three thousand feet over New York.
Just 208 seconds later, the jet was floating in the Hudson River.
The cause was a flock of Canada geese.
The engines were tested against birds of about four pounds.
Two engines, both beyond their design limit, at the same moment.
The pilots' calm turned an engineering failure into a survival story.

aciklama:
On January 15, 2009, US Airways Flight 1549 lost both engines to Canada geese minutes after takeoff. 208 seconds later it ditched in the Hudson; all 155 survived.
